key_insight: Combining doubly robust estimation with linear programming selects cross-border fulfillment centers that reduce delivery time by 8.5–51.1% and logistics cost by 4.4–48.3% versus expert-defined policies.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports cross-border sourcing decisions that balance speed, cost, profit, and shipped volume while keeping the domestic network fixed.
method: Forecast demand and shipping outcomes for source–destination arcs.
Use doubly robust estimation to estimate alternative fulfillment outcomes.
Apply linear programming to select source fulfillment centers across competing objectives.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used 12 months of shipment data across three production-scale international corridors, combining aggregate offline replay with shipment-level counterfactual nearest-neighbor matching.
watch_item: Offline counterfactual results require prospective validation before assuming the same gains under live demand and operational conditions.
paper_title: Cross-Border Fulfillment Center Selection via Doubly Robust Estimation and Linear Programming
